issues.description: The solution implementation references the symbol 'display_start' (e.g. add eax, display_start and mov esi, display_start) but does not define or allocate it. The template declares display_start in .bss (display_start RESB 8294400) and the problem statement explicitly refers to display_start as the framebuffer base. This discrepancy (solution missing the display_start allocation while template and problem expect it) will cause compilation/link errors and confuse students about where the framebuffer base should come from.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore a proper definition/allocation of display_start in the solution (e.g. add 'display_start RESB 8294400' in the .bss section) or, if display_start is intentionally moved to the stack as the solution's comment suggests, update the code to actually allocate and reference that stack-based buffer consistently (and remove global references). Ensure the symbol is defined where referenced so students see a consistent framebuffer base as described in the problem statement.
